description: Signature evidence. Signatures are demoted, never deleted, so these patterns only need to be good enough to collapse a trailing block. The RFC 3676 delimiter is the only high confidence rule; everything else is positional evidence that the sequence classifier weighs.

phrases.pattern: ^\s*(Von meinem|Envoy. de mon|Enviado desde mi|Inviato da|Verzonden vanaf mijn|Skickat från min|Lähetetty|Saadetud minu|Отправлено с) .{0,60}$

^\s*(Best regards|Kind regards|Warm regards|Best wishes|Regards|Cheers|Thanks|Thank you|Sincerely|Best|Yours( sincerely| truly)?|Mit freundlichen Grüßen|Viele Grüße|Beste Grüße|Cordialement|Bien à vous|Saludos|Atentamente|Cordiali saluti|Groeten|Met vriendelijke groet|Med vänliga hälsningar|Vänliga hälsningar|Mvh|Ystävällisin terveisin|Terveisin|Parimat|Parimate soovidega|Heade soovidega|Lugupidamisega|Tervitades|Tervitused|Terv|Kõike head|Ilusat päeva|Head aega|Austusega|С уважением|Z poważaniem|Pozdrawiam)\s*[,.!]?\s*$
phrases.comment: Closing greeting. Mined from blocks the reference labelled SIGNATURE that this baseline missed, which is why the Estonian forms are here: the working corpus is roughly ten percent Estonian and those accounted for the largest group of misses.
Continental European corporate footers carry a registered office and company number. These lines are boilerplate, never authored prose.
A street or postal code line in a trailing block. Weak on its own, but it pairs with a name or a closing greeting to identify a corporate signature.
